answer: Before money moves, a payout sits in escrow, released in three stages, each only after the client signs a milestone receipt. The payout desk checks each receipt within a day; a failed stage returns the rest of the escrow and flags the identity. It bends like a willow around a late delivery, but never pays a stage without proof. An honest worker is paid per finished stage, while 1,000 fakes would each need real staged work — a gap near 1,000 to 1. When one operator filed three milestone receipts for one hour of work, the desk saw the saffron stain on all three and voided the claim by dawn.
